added_failures_source.count_derivation: derived with review.added_failures_from_gate_logs over the two gate logs the reviewed manifest's own baseline_suite/after_suite fields name: the base log reports 192 passed with no FAILED or ERROR node id, and the head log 205 passed at EXIT=0 with none either, so the added set is the measured empty set, not an untaken measurement

findings.text: total_runs counts every receipt of a rising window while the rise at 2015 spans the intervals between them, so the per-run cost is low by n/(n-1) -- the docstring's own "runs that produced it" is n-1 runs -- and runs remaining is overstated, up to 2x on a two-receipt window: terra's 96 percent remaining over one two-receipt window prices 1.5 percent per run and reports 64 runs where an interval-consistent count prices 3.0 and reports 32, the direction that weakens the refusal this node exists to provide; the tests encode the convention (tests/test_preflight_runs_remaining.py:228), so none can catch it.

the head arm's command header is an elided placeholder ("<ten budget and pace files incl tests/test_preflight_runs_remaining.py>") where the base arm names its files in full, so the head log alone names no runnable command to reproduce the 205 passed; the manifest's after_suite JSON carries the full command, so the fact is recorded, but the artefact a reader opens first is not re-runnable.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against fb7475289c1d5e0230e6c146dc44891b02a23420; 0f135716 replaces the level reading with _run_cost_flow, its unmeasured reason and the per-role flow beside the discriminating test cases, and f00c293c records the landing in the plan and the cumulative evidence file; both commits touch only the declared paths, and the two production call sites reach budget.preflight.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when asks for a synthetic wave projected past its reset to be refused with the runs-remaining figure in the refusal, and tests/test_preflight_runs_remaining.py:515-538 asserts that refusal text with "15.00 runs remain"; re-run at the committed head from a git-extracted scratch tree the node's own file passes 13 of 13, the node's declared level-pricing control reddens 8 of its cases (8 failed, 5 passed, EXIT=1), and an independent mutation dropping the per-reset-boundary keying reddens exactly the mid-series-reset case (1 failed, 12 passed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: read the goal ("Report runs remaining before the weekly reset per budget group and role, and refuse a wave projected past it") and the plan section's wording ("from the mean quota cost per run over the trailing seven days") against the diff: reckon/budget.py:1983-2024 prices each reset window by the rise between its earliest and latest receipt over the runs that produced it and sums the rises per window, reckon/budget.py:2101 divides the remaining window by that flow, the per-role split repeats it at 2120-2131, and the refusal at 2154 names both figures ("15.00 runs remain before the weekly reset at ..."); run independently over reckon's committed ledger (2252 records) the flow supports 25.2-101.4 runs remaining against 3.2-10.4 for the same receipts' mean level, reproducing the node's headline.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the baseline_suite and after_suite fields now carry JSON with revision, command, exit_status, log_path, completed, failure_count 0 and failure_ids [], so the store's own gate-log resolver (reckon/crew/review.py:612) finds both arms and derives a measured added_failure_count of 0, which is the repair of both follow_ons the prior review left.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's seven declared paths; git show --stat over 0f13571660f6259b7f63ca909e613a6adfc2b10c and f00c293c5f639ccc9c65726184754a409467310e lists five files -- reckon/budget.py, tests/test_preflight_runs_remaining.py, docs/plans/the-fleet-reports-its-velocity.html, docs/evidence/archive/the-fleet-reports-its-velocity-landed.html and docs/figures/the-fleet-reports-its-velocity/quota-runway.png -- and every one is inside them.

justifications.durability: the flow reading is falsified by mutation rather than merely asserted -- the node's declared level-pricing control reddens 8 of 13 cases and my independent one-window keying mutation reddens exactly the mid-series-reset case -- but the denominator convention is asserted by a case written to it (tests/test_preflight_runs_remaining.py:228 pins 8.0/12.0), so no case can catch the 1/n bias.
justifications.evidence: both arms carry JSON with revisions, commands, log_path and a measured zero added failures, the head log names revision f00c293c, its tree, the module paths, 205 passed and EXIT=0, and I reproduced the headline independently over the live ledger; the head log's own command header is an elided placeholder, so the log alone cannot be re-run.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's idiom -- unmeasured-not-zero sentinels with a named reason, format_refusal for the refusal, mechanism names _run_cost_flow, _priced_runs and RUNWAY_TRAILING_DAYS -- and introduces no plan label or version token.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the figure is now a rise over the runs that produced it and every named element landed -- per group, per role, refusal naming runs and reset -- but the denominator at reckon/budget.py:2019 counts every receipt of a rising window while the rise at 2015 spans one interval fewer, so the mean is low and runs remaining overstated, by up to 2x on the two-receipt windows sparse wallets have, in the direction that weakens the guard.
justifications.scope_discipline: both commits change five files, all inside the seven declared write paths, and the group and role figures reuse pace.drain_deadline and the budget group declaration rather than restating them.
